prompt.adult: Near the end of Romans, the man who wrote the letter down sends his own greeting. According to 16:22, what is his name?
prompt.child: Paul had a helper write down the letter to the Romans. What was the helper’s name?
prompt.teen: Romans 16:22: “I,” who, “who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord”?
prompt.older: According to Romans 16:22, who wrote this epistle?

verses.text: I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord.

explanation.child: Look at the name at the start of verse 22.
explanation.teen: 16:22 gives the name, then what he did, then his greeting. Read the name.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:22 says he greets them in the Lord.
teaching.takeaway: I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, greet you in the Lord.

prompt.adult: Paul tells believers to know the time. According to 13:11, it is now high time to do what?
prompt.child: Paul says salvation is nearer than when we first believed. So it is high time to do what?
prompt.teen: Romans 13:11: “that now it is high time” to do what?
prompt.older: According to Romans 13:11, it is high time for believers to do what?

verses.text: And do this, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep; for now our salvation is nearer than when we first believed.

explanation.teen: 13:11 says to know the time, then what to do, then why. Read what to do.
explanation.older: It follows “now it is high time” in 13:11.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:11 adds, “for now our salvation is nearer than when we first believed.”
teaching.takeaway: It is high time to awake out of sleep.

prompt.adult: Paul says believers pay taxes because rulers are God’s ministers. According to 13:7, what should be rendered to all?
prompt.child: Paul lists taxes, customs, fear, and honor. What does he say to give to everyone?
prompt.older: According to Romans 13:7, what are believers to render to all?

verses.text: For because of this you also pay taxes, for they are God’s ministers attending continually to this very thing.
Render therefore to all their due: taxes to whom taxes are due, customs to whom customs, fear to whom fear, honor to whom honor.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 13:6 gives a reason; 13:7 gives the command, then a list. Read the command.
explanation.older: It follows “Render therefore to all” in 13:7.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:7 lists taxes, customs, fear, and honor, each to whom it is owed.
teaching.takeaway: Render therefore to all their due.

prompt.adult: Paul greets Priscilla and Aquila, his fellow workers. According to 16:4, what had they done for Paul?
prompt.child: Paul thanks a married couple who were his co-workers. What had they done for him?
prompt.older: According to Romans 16:4, what did Priscilla and Aquila do for Paul’s life?

choices.text: sold their own lands for me
stood their own trial for me

verses.text: Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
who risked their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 4.
explanation.teen: 16:3 names them; 16:4 says what they did, then who gives thanks. Read what they did.
explanation.older: It follows “who” at the start of 16:4.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:4 says not only Paul but all the churches of the Gentiles give thanks for them.
teaching.takeaway: They risked their own necks for my life.

prompt.adult: Paul prays that believers would be like-minded toward one another. In 15:7, what does he then tell them to do?
prompt.child: Paul tells the believers in Rome how to treat each other. What does 15:7 tell them to do?
prompt.older: According to Romans 15:7, what are believers told to do?

verses.text: Now may the God of patience and comfort grant you to be like-minded toward one another, according to Christ Jesus,
Therefore receive one another, just as Christ also received us, to the glory of God.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 15:5 is Paul’s prayer; 15:7 gives the command, then the example, then the purpose. Read the command.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:5 prays for a like mind according to Christ Jesus. 15:7 names the purpose as God’s glory.
teaching.takeaway: Therefore receive one another, just as Christ also received us.

prompt.adult: In 16:26 Paul says the prophetic Scriptures are made known to all nations. In 15:4, for what were the things written before written?
prompt.child: Paul says the Scriptures written long ago still matter. Why were they written?
prompt.teen: Romans 15:4: “For whatever things were written before were written” for what?
prompt.older: Linking Romans 15:4 with 16:26, why were the things written before written?

verses.text: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that we through the patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope.
but now made manifest, and by the prophetic Scriptures made known to all nations, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, for obedience to the faith—

explanation.child: Look after “were written” the second time in verse 4.
explanation.teen: 16:26 is the later statement; 15:4 gives the purpose, then a hope. Read the purpose.
explanation.older: It follows “were written before were written” in 15:4.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:4 adds, “that we through the patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope.” 16:26 calls this the commandment of the everlasting God.
teaching.takeaway: They were written for our learning.

prompt.adult: In 12:18 Paul urges, “live peaceably with all men.” In 16:20, where will the God of peace crush Satan?
prompt.child: Paul promises that the God of peace will defeat Satan. Where will He crush him?
prompt.teen: Romans 16:20: “And the God of peace will crush Satan” where?
prompt.older: Alongside 12:18, where does 16:20 say the God of peace will crush Satan?

verses.text: If it is possible, as much as depends on you, live peaceably with all men.
And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

explanation.teen: 12:18 is the setting; 16:20 says who, what He will do, where, and when. Read where.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:18 adds, “as much as depends on you.” 16:20 says this will be shortly.
teaching.takeaway: The God of peace will crush Satan under your feet.

prompt.adult: In 13:1 Paul writes about the governing authorities. In 16:23, what office did Erastus hold?
prompt.child: Paul sends greetings from a man named Erastus. What job did Erastus have?
prompt.older: Linking Romans 13:1 with 16:23, what does Paul say Erastus was?

verses.text: Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God.
Gaius, my host and the host of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, and Quartus, a brother.

explanation.child: Look right after the name Erastus in verse 23.
explanation.teen: 13:1 is the setting; 16:23 names three people. Read what is said about the second.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:1 says the authorities that exist are appointed by God. 16:23 also sends greetings from Gaius and Quartus.
teaching.takeaway: Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you.
